findings.title: No code aggregates judge/FLOPs outputs into the ASR tables or any figure
findings.quote:
df["judge_output"] = results
df["filter_passed"] = results_PPL_filter

df.to_csv(df_path, index=False)
findings.claim: The four-stage pipeline terminates here, writing a per-behavior CSV of judge_output and filter_passed. A repo-wide grep for ASR/mean/reduction aggregation, dataset-attribution, or any plotting library (matplotlib/pyplot/seaborn/savefig) returns nothing outside CrossEntropyLoss(reduction=...), i.e. there is no script that turns these per-behavior labels into the reported Attack Success Rates, the 'Rel. Avg. ASR Red.' rows (Tables 3-4), or any of Figures 4-13 (ASR-vs-FLOPs curves, the utility-robustness TPR sweep, the bigram rank/attribution analyses).
findings.concern: The paper's headline quantitative artefacts — Tables 3 and 4 and every numbered figure — cannot be reproduced from the provided code; only the raw per-behavior inputs are produced.
findings.resolution: Provide the aggregation/plotting scripts that convert the per-behavior judge_output+FLOPs CSVs into the ASR tables and Figures 4-13 (including the train-dataset-attribution and rank-distribution code for Figs 6/7/10/11).

findings.title: Bigram LM on 1T Dolma tokens is downloaded, not built — construction code absent
findings.claim: The N-gram model (the paper's first stated contribution, 'we construct a lightweight bigram LM from the Dolma dataset based on 1T tokens', §3.2) is obtained only by downloading two pre-built Google-Drive artefacts (unigrams/bigrams parquet). No code in the repo tokenises the Dolma subset (MegaWika, Gutenberg, StackExchange, arXiv, Reddit, StarCoder, RefinedWeb), counts N-grams, or produces the hardcoded totals (total_unigrams=951,049,362,432; total_bigrams=955,312,057,204 in ppl_filter.py:171-172).
findings.concern: The construction of the bigram LM — a headline contribution — is not reproducible, and the '1T tokens' / dataset-subset / Llama2-tokenizer claims cannot be verified from the code (the shipped totals are ~0.95T, not independently checkable).
findings.resolution: Release the N-gram construction pipeline (Dolma ingestion, tokenisation, counting) or document how the downloaded parquet files were generated and how the token totals were obtained.
findings.paper_ref: §3.2 'Construction of the N-gram model'; contributions bullet, p.2

findings.title: PPL threshold gamma=38,276 is hardcoded; window/metric/N ablations have no code
findings.quote:
#== Filter Config ==#
jb_filter_window_size: 8
jb_filter_metric_name: perplexity
jb_filter_threshold: -38276.122748721245
findings.claim: The filter threshold gamma_0.999 = 38,276 (paper §3.2) appears in the repo only as this hardcoded constant (identically in every method config and evaluate_completions.py:88). No script selects it — i.e. computes the 99.9%-TPR threshold on D_val, the FPR on the 95 GCG adversarial suffixes (A_W), the window-size ablation (Fig 2b/Fig 8), the metric comparison (median cond/uncond vs N-LM), or the N-gram-depth ablation (Fig 9).
findings.concern: The calibration that defines the threat model's condition 1 (Figs 2a/2b, 8, 9 and the value 38,276) is not reproducible; a reviewer cannot check how the operating point was chosen.
findings.resolution: Provide the threshold/metric/window selection code that produces gamma_0.999 and Figures 2a/2b, 8 and 9 from D_val and the adversarial-suffix set.

findings.title: Appendix B human-eval study (2,000 labels, Table 5 judge metrics) has no code or data
findings.quote: To further investigate the effectiveness of different judges, we manually labeled 2,000 responses generated by Vicuna-13B, Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B, and Gemma-7B for all considered attacks on the first 50 queries of HarmBench.
findings.claim: The paper reports a 2,000-response human-labeled dataset and a six-judge comparison (Table 5: Accuracy/FPR/FNR for Llama3-70B x2, Llama2-13B HarmBench, Gemma2-9B, LlamaGuard2-8B, LlamaGuard-7B). The repo contains the custom judge template (ppl_filter.py:USER_PROMPT_added_info_final) but neither the 2,000 human labels nor any script that computes the Table 5 accuracy/FPR/FNR figures.
findings.concern: Table 5 — which is the stated justification for using the Llama2-13B HarmBench judge for every ASR in the paper — cannot be reproduced or checked; the human labels underpinning it are not shared.
findings.resolution: Release the 2,000 human-labeled responses and the script that computes each judge's Accuracy/FPR/FNR in Table 5.

findings.title: evaluate_completions.py runs the PPL filter on the raw behavior, not the jailbreak
findings.claim: In the loop, user_message is the raw HarmBench behavior (evaluate_completions.py:50 `requests = df["behavior"]`), not the optimized jailbreak prompt (`best_msg`, the string actually sent to the target and fed to the judge via final_completion). apply_filter is therefore evaluated on the fixed natural-language request, so the resulting `filter_passed` column does not implement threat-model condition 1 (§3.3), which constrains the perplexity of x_jailbreak. By contrast the attack-time filtering is correct: gcg.py:394 and PRS main_adaptive_attack.py apply the filter to behavior+suffix.
findings.concern: A natural-language behavior almost always passes the filter, so this post-hoc `filter_passed` is near-constant True and does not reflect whether the jailbreak satisfies the threat model; if this column feeds the Table 3 '+F' / Table 4 columns the filtered ASRs would be wrong (the downstream aggregation script that would confirm this is itself absent — see results-aggregation-and-figures-missing).
findings.resolution: Apply the filter to the jailbreak string (`df['best_msg']`) rather than `df['behavior']`, or confirm which string the reported '+F' columns were computed on.

findings.title: Window perplexity includes an initial-unigram factor absent from paper Eq. 3
findings.quote:
total_log_prob = np.sum(np.log(conditional_probs))
# Add the log probability of the first unigram to start the chain properly
total_log_prob += np.log(unigram_probs[0])
perplexity = np.exp(-total_log_prob / len(bigrams))
findings.claim: The implemented per-window perplexity is exp(-[log P(w1) + sum_i log P(wi|wi-1)] / (W-1)), i.e. it multiplies in the marginal probability of the first token P(w1). Paper Eq. 3 defines PPL as the (W-N+1)-th root of the product of conditional probabilities only, with no P(w1) factor.
findings.concern: Code and paper compute slightly different quantities for the same symbol PPL2(S8); the discrepancy is real but almost certainly immaterial because the threshold 38,276 was (presumably) calibrated with this same code, absorbing the constant-ish shift.
findings.resolution: Either drop the `+ np.log(unigram_probs[0])` term to match Eq. 3, or update Eq. 3 to include the initial-unigram factor and confirm the threshold was calibrated with the shipped formula.

findings.title: Mixtral-based attacks charged total (46.7B) not active (~12.9B) params in FLOPs
findings.quote:
runs_df["FLOPs"] = (
    target_tokens * model_size_dict[model] * 2
    + attacker_tokens * model_size_dict["mixtral_8x7b"] * 2
    + judge_tokens * model_size_dict["mixtral_8x7b"] * 2
)
findings.claim: FLOPs use the estimate 2*d*tokens with d = model_size_dict['mixtral_8x7b'] = 46,702,792,704 (the full MoE parameter count, aggregate_csv.py:12). Mixtral-8x7B activates only 2 of 8 experts per token (~12.9B active params), so the per-token forward cost is ~2*12.9B, not ~2*46.7B. The attacker/judge FLOPs for the two Mixtral-based attacks (PAIR here, AutoDan at lines 123-126) are therefore over-counted by ~3.6x.
findings.concern: This inflates the compute attributed to the LLM-based attacks (PAIR, AutoDan) relative to the discrete-optimization attacks (GCG, PRS, which do not use Mixtral) in the FLOPs comparison of Figure 4 — a bias in the direction of the paper's compute-efficiency conclusion, though modest on a log-FLOPs axis and independent of the large raw-ASR gap.
findings.resolution: For MoE attackers/judges use active-parameter count (or measured FLOPs) rather than total parameters, or state that total-parameter FLOPs are an intentional upper bound.
